newsitem.title: CHINA: China calls for stronger grassroots social order.
newsitem.headline: China calls for stronger grassroots social order.

text.p: China has told grassroots public security officials to do more to keep social order and cut crime, the Xinhua Daily Telegraph said on Monday.

Beijing's Central Committee for Comprehensive Management of Public Security had instructed local-level officials to deepen their links with the people and boost cooperation among security agencies, the official newspaper said.
The publication also said it was time for stepped up propaganda work to put a stop to rising crime.

"The masses must be motivated and organised to resolutely struggle against criminals' illegal behaviour, and the chaotic public security situation must be turned around as quickly as possible," it quoted the committee as saying.
Crime has soared in China as social controls weaken in the transition from strict communism to a market-style economy, prompting repeated public security crackdowns.
Management at all levels of public security organisations should be tightened and responsibility clearly allocated among officials, the newspaper said.
Additional manpower, material and financial support should be given to grassroots organisations, who should organise local patrols to protect residential areas, it said.
It quoted the public security committee as saying emphasis should be put on controlling China's huge migrant population, but gave no details.

Many rural labourers leave their farms in search of work in the cities, providing manpower for factories and construction crews. But the mass migration also leads to many social problems when jobs are unavailable.
